clue.text: Father of Ham got into Egypt, wandering

indicators.note: letters that go wandering stray from their places, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's father found his way into Egypt and roamed about there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks biblical (Noah's son, Egypt nearby), but it is Ham in Dickens's David Copperfield, whose uncle and guardian is the Yarmouth fisherman. 'Wandering' mixes GOT and EGYPT.
explanation.definitionFit: In David Copperfield, the boatman Daniel is the adoptive father figure to young Ham, his orphaned nephew.

clue.text: Powerful alkali has top ingredients

indicators.note: ingredients are mixed, so the letters of the two words are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: A caustic chemical is a key component.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium carbonate or hydroxide, a strong caustic base.

clue.text: Open gate, way in for the aristocracy

indicators.note: the opening of gate is its first letter

parts.note: an entry is an entrance

explanation.surface: The manor gate is opened to admit the nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: The landed gentry are the upper classes just below the nobility.

clue.text: Primula in neat border

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, one being an ox
a lip is a rim or edge

explanation.surface: A primrose planted in a tidy flowerbed edging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' reads as tidy but is the archaic noun for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a wild flower of the primrose genus Primula.

clue.text: Ratty takes in one fellow to give evidence

indicators.note: the irritable word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: ratty means irritable, testy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An irritable man lets in a colleague who will be a witness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ratty' looks like the Wind in the Willows character but is just bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: To testify is to bear witness under oath in court.

clue.text: Hang loosely, like elbow at break of day?

indicators.note: the break of day is its very start, so the opening letter of day is taken

parts.note: a bent elbow forms an angle

explanation.surface: A dangling limb, its elbow crooked, as dawn breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle is to hang or swing freely and loosely.

clue.text: Striking, a function of policemen?

explanation.surface: A strike, and what police do about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking catches the eye; detaining suspects is what officers do.

clue.text: Cigar-ring drifting over America? Goodness!

indicators.note: in a down clue the mixed letters sit over the next piece
smoke drifting about rearranges the letters of the word cigar

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A smoke ring floats across America to someone's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Gracious me! is a mild exclamation of surprise, like Goodness me!

clue.text: Instances of having sleep broken around 10 am

indicators.note: the mixed letters go around the time
sleep that is broken is disturbed, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten
taken as written, the morning abbreviation

explanation.surface: Times when one's sleep was disturbed at ten in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Examples are specimens or cases illustrating something.

clue.text: Without air and sun in sleet storm

indicators.note: a storm whirls things about, so the letters of the words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A weather report: no breeze, and the sun lost in a sleet storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' looks like weather, but here it is a melody; 'storm' is the signal to mix the letters, and 'in' merely sets one word inside the other before the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a melody, so lacking one is lacking any tune.

clue.text: Foreign side defeated by English slow bowler

definitions.text: Foreign side defeated by English slow bowler

parts.words: Foreign side defeated by English slow bowler
parts.note: reads like a cricket report of a touring team beaten by spin, but recalls the Spanish fleet of 1588 and Sir Francis Drake, who famously finished his game of bowls first

explanation.surface: A touring cricket team is beaten by an English spinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket terms mislead: the 'slow bowler' is Drake, said to have finished his game of bowls on Plymouth Hoe before sailing out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish fleet sent against England in 1588 was the enemy force Drake helped rout.

clue.text: Relatively long time for silver-points

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
E and S, east and south, are compass points

explanation.surface: Silverpoint drawings take a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is informal for a long while, as in 'I waited for ages'.

clue.text: Robust sticking-plaster

explanation.surface: A sturdy bandage.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapping lad is big and sturdy; strapping is also adhesive plaster tape used to bind injuries.

clue.text: To be really thrifty, take head off pint

parts.note: to skim is to remove the top layer, as froth from beer
P is a standard abbreviation for pint

explanation.surface: A miser blows the froth off his beer to save money.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to economise stingily, using too little.

clue.text: Tarry rope

explanation.surface: A rope coated in tar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tarry' reads as an adjective (covered in tar) but is the verb to linger.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to remain or linger; on a ship a stay is a rope bracing the mast.

clue.text: Perhaps at thrilly stage in match at Wimbledon

indicators.note: perhaps signals one possible arrangement of the letters of the words

explanation.surface: A thrilling moment in a Wimbledon match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrilly' is a made-up word that betrays its role as fodder; Wimbledon is the London tennis championship.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis scoring, each player having won two points in a game.

clue.text: Attack and capture

explanation.surface: A military raid that takes prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit or stroke is an attack of illness; a seizing of goods or territory is a capture.

clue.text: Suave girl coming out elated…

parts.note: a deb, or debutante, is a girl coming out into society
walking on air means elated

explanation.surface: A smooth young woman thrilled to be making her society debut.
explanation.walkthrough: A debutante was a young upper-class woman formally presented to British society, said to 'come out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A debonair man is charming and smoothly confident.

clue.text: Balfe's girl, in unconventional style

explanation.surface: An opera heroine with an unorthodox life.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Balfe wrote the 1843 opera The Bohemian Girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Balfe's opera title names its heroine thus; the word also means artistic and free of social convention.

clue.text: Feeling of excitement from Euclid's first proposition

indicators.note: the first of the word Euclid's is its opening letter

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put forward for debate

explanation.surface: A thrill at reading the first theorem in Euclid's geometry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proposition' suggests a geometric theorem, but it is a motion put to a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong feeling or agitation of the mind, such as joy or anger.

clue.text: Variety of hens sensitive to the cold

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of hens take another order

explanation.surface: A breed of chicken that cannot stand the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a Northern English dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Northern English dialect a nesh person feels the cold easily and is soft.

clue.text: Got a new robe for Julius Caesar?

indicators.note: a new version of the words is a reshaping of their letters

explanation.surface: Someone bought a fresh gown to dress as Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: The draped woollen outer garment worn by Roman citizens.

clue.text: Finger-protector used in rigging?

explanation.surface: A sewing aid among a ship's ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewing cap for the fingertip; also a metal ring spliced into a rope's eye in ship's rigging.

clue.text: Students' fun abroad, St making stew?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as "Students' fun abroad, St making stew?": RAG + OUT gives the answer, but 'St' has no job and looks like an OCR misreading not found in any source
annotationWithheld.clue: Students' fun abroad, St making stew?

clue.text: South-eastern, coyly playful ferret

parts.note: arch means mischievously coy

explanation.surface: A frisky ferret from the south-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ferret' looks like the animal but is the verb, to hunt about.
explanation.definitionFit: To ferret out is to hunt or rummage about looking for something.

clue.text: Observable, endless poverty?

indicators.note: with no ends means the first and last letters of poverty are dropped

explanation.surface: Is grinding poverty there for all to see?
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, not hidden.

clue.text: Vessel carrying phantom, Bristol fashion

indicators.note: the vessel carries the next piece along behind it in the same word

parts.note: a ship is a sea-going vessel
a shape can be a ghostly apparition

explanation.surface: A ghost ship sailing out of the port of Bristol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shipshape and Bristol fashion' is a British idiom for neat and in good order, from the tidy ships of Bristol's harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom pairs the two phrases as synonyms for trim and orderly.

clue.text: Leading on court system

parts.note: a set is a unit of play in a tennis match on court
up means ahead, as in one up

explanation.surface: Being in the lead on a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A setup is an arrangement or organisation of things.

clue.text: Creature with plate on its back

indicators.note: something lying on its back is turned over, so the word for plate is read backwards

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: A tortoise with its shell plate on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: Any living being, such as a beast, is a creature.

clue.text: Premises engaged in final stock reduction

definitions.text: Premises engaged in final stock reduction

parts.words: Premises engaged in final stock reduction
parts.note: sounds like a shop holding a closing-down sale, but the stock is livestock, reduced for the last time by slaughter

explanation.surface: A shop holding its last clearance sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterhouse is where farm animals are killed, ending their lives as livestock.

clue.text: Right leg joint feel sore?

parts.note: the ankle joins leg to foot

explanation.surface: Does my right ankle feel sore?
explanation.definitionFit: A slight that rankles continues to cause resentment, so to rankle is to remain bitter.

clue.text: Bulletin roughly pasted to front of church

indicators.note: the mixed letters are attached before the next piece
done roughly, the word is put together carelessly, so its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A notice stuck hastily on the church door.
explanation.definitionFit: A despatch is an official message or news report sent from the field.
